1.say: Twist the orange caps off the house wires. Pull the two white wires and the two black wires out of the gray box.
placements: orange twist cap → unscrewed off the white and black house wires and set clear of the gray wall box (in the video: held in the right hand at the right edge of the frame)

white insulated house wire with bare copper tip → pulled out to hang outside the gray plastic wall box one on the left side and one on the right side of the opening (in the video: left and right sides of the box opening on the white wall)
black insulated house wire with bare copper tip → pulled out to hang outside the gray plastic wall box in the middle of the opening (in the video: center and upper right of the box opening)
bare ground wires → cut short and pushed to the bottom back inside the gray wall box away from the four bare ends (in the video: bottom inside of the box)
watch_for: If a bare copper end stays hidden inside the box, you did not pull that wire out far enough.
If an orange cap is still on a wire, that wire is not exposed and will test wrong.
1.check_yourself: Four bare copper ends stick out of the gray box with no caps on.
1.safety: Switch the breaker off before you touch any bare wire.

2.say: Touch the red and black probes to the bare copper ends. Check the yellow tester body shows no power.
placements: red probe tip of the yellow tester → touched against the bare copper end of a house wire inside the gray wall box opening (in the video: bottom of the box opening)
black probe tip of the yellow tester → touched against the bare copper end of another house wire inside the gray wall box opening beside the red probe (in the video: bottom of the box opening)
watch_for: If you touch the two probes together, the tester can beep and fake a live reading.
If a probe touches plastic insulation instead of bare copper, dead can look safe when it is not.
2.check_yourself: The yellow tester probes touch the bare wires and the tester shows no power.
2.safety: Keep your fingers behind the probe handles and off the bare copper.

3.say: Gather the two white house wires together. Twist the bare ends together, then screw the yellow nut on tight. Push the capped white wires to the back of the gray box.
placements: white insulated house wire with bare copper tip → twisted together with the second white insulated house wire in front of the gray wall box (in the video: center of the frame in front of the box opening)
yellow twist nut → screwed clockwise over both twisted white bare ends until tight using fingers (in the video: lower center of the box opening)
capped white wires with yellow nut → pushed to the back bottom inside the gray plastic wall box leaving only black wires out (in the video: tucked inside the lower back of the box)
watch_for: If white copper shows below the yellow nut, the nut is not screwed on far enough.
If a white wire slips out when you tug, the twist was loose and needs redoing.
3.check_yourself: The two white wires disappear under a yellow nut tucked inside the box leaving two black wires out.
3.safety: Keep the breaker off so the white wires stay dead while you twist.

4.say: Hold the black thermostat base below the gray box. Twist one black thermostat lead to the first black wall wire. Screw the red nut over the joined ends.
placements: black rectangular thermostat base with white round knob and two black leads → held hanging below the gray wall box on the white wall (in the video: below and to the right of the box opening)
black thermostat lead with bare end → twisted together with the first black wall wire with bare copper tip in front of the gray box (in the video: center of the box opening)
red twist nut → screwed clockwise over the first black wall wire and thermostat lead joint using fingers (in the video: inside the upper part of the box opening)
watch_for: If you join the thermostat lead to a white wire, you picked the wrong wall wire and must redo it.
If bare copper shows below the red nut, the red nut is not tight and can slip off.
4.check_yourself: One black wall wire is capped with a red nut to the hanging thermostat while the other black wire waits.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off while you handle the black wires and the red nut.

5.say: Twist the last black wall wire to the last black thermostat lead. Screw the second red nut over the joined ends. Let the black thermostat base hang below the gray box.
placements: last black wall wire with bare copper tip → twisted together with the last free black thermostat lead in front of the gray box (in the video: upper right of the box opening)
second red twist nut → screwed clockwise over the second black joint until no copper shows using fingers (in the video: upper center of the box opening)
black thermostat base with white knob → left hanging by its two connected black leads below the gray wall box (in the video: hanging below the box on the right side of the frame)
watch_for: If you reuse the first red nut for both joints, one joint will be loose and can overheat.
If the two black joints touch each other outside the nuts, they can short when power returns.
5.check_yourself: Both black wall wires are capped to the thermostat leads and the thermostat hangs from the box.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off because single pole wiring can leave one side hot.

6.say: Push the capped wires into the gray box. Hold the black thermostat base flat over the wall opening. Drive the top and bottom screws tight.
placements: capped wire joints with red and yellow nuts → pushed folded into the back of the gray plastic wall box (in the video: tucked inside the box opening behind the thermostat base)

black rectangular thermostat base with white round knob → held centered flat over the gray wall box opening on the white wall with knob facing out (in the video: center right of the frame covering the opening)
silver mounting screw → driven through the top mounting hole of the thermostat base into the top screw hole of the gray box with a power driver (in the video: top center of the black base)
silver mounting screw → driven through the bottom mounting hole of the thermostat base into the bottom screw hole of the gray box with a power driver (in the video: bottom center of the black base)
watch_for: If the base rocks when you push it, wires are trapped behind it and need repacking.
If the base sits crooked, the top and bottom screw holes are not aligned square to the wall.
6.check_yourself: The black thermostat base with white knob is screwed flat over the wall opening.
6.safety: Keep the breaker off while you push the wires in and drive the screws.

7.say: Align the white square cover over the black base. Push the cover straight on until it clicks.
placements: white square plastic cover with round dial and vent slots → pushed straight onto the black thermostat base centered on the white wall (in the video: center right of the frame covering the black base)
watch_for: If the cover will not sit flat, the white knob is misaligned and blocks the dial.
If the cover falls off when you let go, it is not pushed on far enough to catch.
7.check_yourself: A white Honeywell cover with dial sits centered on the white wall.
